conflicts: Brief Alignment proposes: Keep the current title/menu composition and pixel-synthwave identity, but make all four highway lanes visibly continuous from horizon to receptors using subtle yet unmistakable separators. Literal completeness alone can yield a checklist-like screen unless required content is transformed into content-specific visual storytelling. Clarity proposes: Keep the title as the first read, make Start the clear second read, and slightly reduce the sunset/demo-score cluster so attention then moves naturally into the highway. Aggressive simplification and a single predictable focal path can make the result safe, uniform, and forgettable. Visual System & Craft proposes: Create a strict effects hierarchy: reserve the strongest glow for the hit line and active note, reduce background scanline/particle/grid opacity, and use one controlled chromatic offset on the title. Over-standardizing geometry, color, component construction, and effects risks flattening semantically different roles into the same generic treatment.
accept: Accept all requested content, a readable focal structure, and a disciplined shared craft system as constraints. Accept reduced arbitrary effects and consistent secondary components, provided the hero, important states, and meaningfully different content roles retain distinctive visual treatment.
compromise: Preserve the content-motivated expressive action: Tie each lane to a distinct instrument or dance cue through restrained symbols and note behaviors, integrate the title rhythmically with the highway perspective, and add one signature hit-line burst or dancer silhouette that makes this game recognizable beyond standard synthwave conventions. Build it with Craft's shared tokens, place it within Clarity's dominant/secondary structure, and attach it directly to Brief Alignment's requested roles. Keep supporting UI restrained, but allow the hero and semantically different states purposeful variation in scale, silhouette, texture, or color; reject random decoration and generic uniformity alike.
